title: Hardy–Weinberg and population structure
summary: Genotype frequencies under random mating, and the heterozygote deficit that pooling structured populations creates (Wahlund effect).

children.label: Allele
children.description: One version of the variant (reference or alternative).

children.label: Genotype
children.description: The pair of alleles a person carries: homozygous or heterozygous.

children.label: Allele frequency
children.description: p, the share of the alternative allele in a sample.

concepts.label: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
concepts.description: Under random mating genotypes come in p², 2pq, q².

facts.text: Stated independently by G. H. Hardy and Wilhelm Weinberg in 1908.

concepts.label: Population structure
concepts.description: Mating within groups whose allele frequencies differ.

children.label: Population
children.description: A 1000 Genomes population and its sampling site.

children.label: Wahlund effect
children.description: Pooled samples show a heterozygote deficit equal to F_ST.

children.label: Fixation index (F_ST)
children.description: Variance of allele frequency between populations over p̄(1 − p̄).

concepts.label: Natural selection
concepts.description: Why these variants' frequencies differ, and for HbS why heterozygotes are in excess.

children.label: Heterozygote advantage
children.description: Carriers of HbS are protected from severe malaria.

facts.text: Sickle-cell trait protects against severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
